title: Four Lengths and a Pause
story: Greta had swum for years, yet a sore shoulder made her usual crawl stroke impossible. The pool coach watched two lengths and asked her to stop before she began to compensate with her neck. He suggested breaststroke for a fortnight, with a kickboard on days when even that pull hurt. Greta felt embarrassed, because the slow lane was full of beginners and she had once trained with the club squad. The coach said fitness could be protected in more than one way, and that pride was a poor reason to delay healing. By the second week her shoulder ached less in the morning, and she could dress without a careful shrug. She still avoided diving. At the end of the fortnight the coach let her swim four lengths of crawl, then return to the gentler stroke if the ache came back. Greta learned that pausing a habit was different from losing it.

vocabulary.definition: To make up for a weak part by using another.
A swimming stroke with both arms moving together.

quiz.question: What swimming plan did the coach give Greta?
options: Breaststroke for two weeks, and a kickboard if the pull hurt
Crawl only, so the sore shoulder would toughen
Diving practice with the club squad
No swimming until she felt no awkwardness
quiz.correctAnswer: Breaststroke for two weeks, and a kickboard if the pull hurt
quiz.explanation: He suggested breaststroke for a fortnight, and a kickboard on days when the pull hurt.
quiz.supportingSentence: He suggested breaststroke for a fortnight, with a kickboard on days when even that pull hurt.

quiz.question: What was Greta allowed to try at the end of that period?
options: Four lengths of crawl, then the gentler stroke if pain returned
A full squad session with dives
Two lengths using her neck to help the arm
Nothing further, even if the morning felt better
quiz.correctAnswer: Four lengths of crawl, then the gentler stroke if pain returned
quiz.explanation: The coach let her swim four lengths of crawl, then return to the gentler stroke if the ache came back.
quiz.supportingSentence: At the end of the fortnight the coach let her swim four lengths of crawl, then return to the gentler stroke if the ache came back.

quiz.question: Why did the slow lane embarrass Greta?
options: She was swimming among beginners after once training with the squad
The coach told her she would never swim again
The kickboard was forbidden in that lane
Her neck pain had started among the beginners
quiz.correctAnswer: She was swimming among beginners after once training with the squad
quiz.explanation: She felt embarrassed because the slow lane was full of beginners and she had trained with the squad.
quiz.supportingSentence: Greta felt embarrassed, because the slow lane was full of beginners and she had once trained with the club squad.

quiz.question: What idea did Greta take from the two weeks?
options: Stopping a habit for a while is not the same as losing it
A sore shoulder means a swimmer should quit
Pride is a good reason to swim through pain
Four lengths of crawl replace every other stroke
quiz.correctAnswer: Stopping a habit for a while is not the same as losing it
quiz.explanation: She learned that pausing a habit was different from losing it.
quiz.supportingSentence: Greta learned that pausing a habit was different from losing it.

quiz.question: What does compensate mean here?
options: Let another part of the body take over the work
Swim faster than the club squad
Rest for a period of two weeks
Feel awkward in front of beginners
quiz.correctAnswer: Let another part of the body take over the work
quiz.explanation: The coach stopped her before she could compensate with her neck, meaning use her neck to do the shoulder's work.
quiz.supportingSentence: The pool coach watched two lengths and asked her to stop before she began to compensate with her neck.
